newsitem.title: POLAND: HANDLOWY STABLE INVESTOR DEAL SEEN JULY.
newsitem.headline: HANDLOWY STABLE INVESTOR DEAL SEEN JULY.

text.p: Poland should conclude its sale of a 24-percent stake in Bank Handlowy SA to three so-called stable-investors next month, the bank's president said on Monday.

Last week the state treasury signed a sale agreement with JP Morgan , Swedbank and Zurich Insurance in which they would acquire 24 percent of Handlowy's capital diluted by its 28-million convertible bond issue.

The conclusion of the transaction however required relevant permits from the Polish and U.S. central banks and agreements on the distribution of power in the supervisory board, Cezary Stypulkowski told a news conference.
"We expect this (the conclusion of the transaction) to happen in July," Stypulkowski said.

Under the sale agreement JP Morgan and its subsidiaries would buy 9,602,500 shares and 1,557,500 convertible bonds representing 12 percent of Handlowy. Zurich Insurance Co or its subsidiaries and Swedbank would get six-percent stakes each.
The three investors agreed to hold Handlowy securities for minimum periods of between 540 days and three years.
Artur Nieradko, Handlowy director in charge of privatisation, also present, said that in the bank's 19.5- million-share institutional tranche the bank's shares were allotted to 200 investors.
He said equally-sized 30 percent portions of the institutional offer went to U.S. and British investors.
Polish institutions have been allotted 400,000 shares, Nieradko added.
